title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X/S is smooth of relative dimension 1, so that ω = Ω^1_{X/S} is invertible. Judging from the surrounding pages, the data are:
- a rank-2 bundle (called L or V; the notation shifts between pages);
- a line subbundle Ω = Fil_1 (a Hodge-type filtration), equivalently a section σ of the associated P^1-bundle P → X;
- a connection c relative to S.

The component c_{2,3}. This is the composite Ω → (rank 2)⊗ω → (quotient)⊗ω. Grothendieck rewrites it as a map Ω → ω using the identification Ω ≅ σ*(Ω^1_{P/X}). The latter is Hom(line, quotient)^∨ up to twist: the relative cotangent space of the projective bundle along the section. Through this identification, c_{2,3} is the derivative of the section σ with respect to the projective connection induced by c. It is the Kodaira–Spencer / second fundamental form of the filtration.

Definitions.
- σ (the flag) is 'nowhere stationary' for c if c_{2,3} is everywhere non-zero, i.e. it makes Ω a local direct factor of ω.
- Since both are line bundles, this means c_{2,3} is an isomorphism. Such connections are called 'transverse' to the flag.
- He then rigidifies by fixing an isomorphism i: Ω ≅ ω and considering only connections with c_{2,3} = i. These form a torsor ('Conn^transv(V,i)'), stated to be under L⊗ω.

Restriction to Ω. He then restricts c to Ω = Fil_1, c|Ω: Ω → L⊗ω. On the next page this is shown to be a first-order differential operator. It therefore factors through the principal-parts bundle P^1_{X/S}(Ω). The resulting linear map γ is a morphism of extensions:
- on the sub Ω⊗ω it is the identity;
- on the quotient it is −2i;
- so γ is an isomorphism when 2 is invertible.

This recovers the previous page's canonical description L ≅ P^1_{X/S}(ω)⊗ω^{-1}. In modern terms: a rank-2 bundle with a flag and a connection whose Kodaira–Spencer map is an isomorphism is a PGL_2/SL_2-oper (Gunning indigenous bundle, projective structure). Its underlying filtered bundle is canonically a jet bundle, unique up to unique isomorphism. The problem served is the structure of the Gauss–Manin connection on H^1_dR of a family of curves (prototype: elliptic curves, where KS gives ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω^1). The surrounding material (Picard–Fuchs, Cartier operation) is the context.
errors: The claim that transverse connections with c_{2,3}=i form a torsor under 'L⊗ω' is unclear as transcribed. Differences of such connections are End-valued 1-forms θ with θ(Ω)⊂Ω⊗ω, i.e. Borel-valued forms, which have rank 3 (rank 2 if the determinant connection is fixed). Unless L denotes something else or a determinant normalization is implicit, the stated structure group is imprecise.
Notation drifts: L is sometimes the ambient rank-2 bundle (c|Ω: Ω → L⊗ω) and sometimes a line in V ('σ, i.e. L ⊂ V'). This is a notational slip, not a mathematical error.
'facteur direct local de ω' for a map between two line bundles just means isomorphism. The general-rank formulation is not needed here.

ideas.what: Kodaira–Spencer component c_{2,3} of a connection on a filtered rank-2 bundle, interpreted as the derivative of the section σ of the P^1-bundle
ideas.modern_name: second fundamental form / Kodaira–Spencer map of the Hodge filtration; derivative of the period map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (1968), Katz–Oda (1968), Katz (1972) for elliptic curves

ideas.what: Connections 'transverse' to a line subbundle (KS isomorphism, flag nowhere stationary)
ideas.modern_name: SL_2/PGL_2-opers; Gunning's indigenous bundles; projective structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1967), Drinfeld–Sokolov (1985), Beilinson–Drinfeld (1990s), Mochizuki (indigenous bundles in char p, 1990s)

ideas.what: Restriction of a transverse connection to Fil_1 factors through P^1(Ω), giving an isomorphism of extensions with P^1_{X/S}(Ω) when 2 is invertible; the underlying filtered bundle is canonically a jet bundle
ideas.modern_name: the oper bundle is a twisted jet bundle (J^1 of ω^{-1/2} up to twist)

missed.claim: Around 1972, in a manuscript on Gauss–Manin connections and the Cartier operation, Grothendieck defines, over a general base S, connections on a filtered rank-2 bundle that are 'transverse' (KS map an isomorphism, rigidified by i: Ω ≅ ω). He identifies the filtered bundle canonically with principal parts when 2 is invertible. This is the notion of indigenous bundle/oper in arithmetic families, in the same notes as the Cartier operation. That combination is what Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory (dormant indigenous bundles, Frobenius) later systematized.
missed.quote: on dit (si ω est loc. libre de t.f.) que σ (i.e. L ⊂ V) est nulle part stationnaire pour c ... On parlera des connexions "transverses" à V
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early, relative/arithmetic formulation of opers predating Drinfeld–Sokolov and Mochizuki. It is of historical interest for crediting the 'Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism ⇒ canonical jet-bundle structure' viewpoint. It is unlikely to contain mathematics new to specialists today.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is classical in hindsight: opers/indigenous bundles, Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism, jet-bundle normal form. The notable point is that Grothendieck formulated this relatively over S, with attention to the prime 2, alongside the Cartier operation around 1972. That anticipates the framework of Mochizuki's indigenous-bundle theory in unpublished form.
transcription_corrections: '[-Alors-] {+i.e. si [?]+} fait de Ω un facteur direct local de ω' likely reads 'i.e. si elle fait de Ω un facteur direct local de ω'.
'que ω est inv. [?]' is probably 'que Ω est inversible', i.e. Ω of rank 1.
Last line 'Ω ⊗ ω̌ [?], ω' is likely an annotation under the arrow, e.g. 'Ω⊗ω̌, ω' indicating L⊗ω is an extension of ω by Ω⊗ω (as used on the next page).
